clue.text: Illusionist takes quiet breather: I like it reaching a peak

taken as written

taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage magician pauses for breath, pleased to have climbed to the top of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky peak, common in the English West Country; 'reaching' just strings the last piece on.
explanation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror whose tricks rely on sleight of hand, so an illusionist.

explanation.definitionFit: A peaches-and-cream complexion is the idiom for fair, rosy, glowing skin that looks healthy.

explanation.walkthrough: A luncheon voucher (LV) was a paper token British employers gave staff to buy lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a freshwater fish caught as it migrates up rivers.

explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace can be a raised open platform or balcony on a building, as in a theatre's upper tiers.

clue.text: Shrink gets led off, restraining flatulence

explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to grow steadily smaller, so it is a synonym of the verb shrink.

clue.text: Shots in the dark being pumped into theatre cat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Re' is the memo word meaning 'concerning'; the definition is 'concerning writing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Textual means relating to a text, so concerning something written.

clue.text: Neglect that's designed to be appealing on box

explanation.walkthrough: The box is British slang for television.

clue.text: Dwarf to rear the Spanish height-enhancer's family

explanation.walkthrough: Rumpelstiltskin is the little man of the Grimm fairy tale who spins straw into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the fairy-tale manikin whose name the miller's daughter must guess, so a dwarf.

clue.text: Run with complacent delight, almost

clue.text: Be prone to romance

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'tend towards love'; 'prone' is the posture sense, and 'romance' the verb for exaggerating.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both lying down flat and telling falsehoods, matching both senses.

clue.text: Stash in quarter of the island

the large Greek island

explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it away, which is what stashing it means.

clue.text: Take care of politician later, including one with a sidekick

Member of Parliament
anon is an old word for soon, later
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take care of' reads as 'look after', but 'care of' is the postal c/o.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion is someone who accompanies another, much as a sidekick is a constant associate.

clue.text: Endlessly follow Japanese fish

clue.text: Sick of one with plates

taken as written

clue.text: Arab, say - so it says here - is about to give out

clue.text: On account of colloquial island
